title: Social insects: ants and bees
keyIdea: Ants and honeybees are social insects: they live together in a big family called a colony and share out the jobs. A honeybee hive has one queen, who lays all the eggs, thousands of female workers, who do every other job, and in summer a few hundred male drones. A worker's job changes as she grows: she cleans and feeds young inside first and flies out for food last. A bee shares where flowers are with a waggle dance, and an ant leaves a scent trail for the others to follow. No one gives orders, not even the queen. Most kinds of bee live alone.
familyTip: On a warm day, put a few crumbs of biscuit near an ant trail and watch from a little way off. Do more ants come over time? Do they walk the same line? Talk about how one ant could tell the others without talking. Then look at bees on flowers and spot the yellow pollen loads on their back legs.

visual.caption: True or not true about ants and bees? Drag each card, or tap it and then a box.

items: Only the queen bee lays eggs

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort hive jobs, follow a worker through her life, read waggle dances, lay an ant scent trail and sort colony insects from loners.

kid: Some insects live on their own. Ants and honeybees live together in a big family called a colony. Every member has a job, and the colony only works when everyone does theirs.

A honeybee hive has one queen. She lays all the eggs, up to 2,000 a day in summer. The workers are all female. They clean, feed the young, build wax comb, guard the door and fetch food. The drones are male. They have no sting and fetch no food.

A worker's job changes as she grows. A young worker stays inside and cleans cells. Later she feeds the young and builds comb. At about three weeks old she guards the door, and then she flies out to fetch nectar and pollen.

Insects in a colony share news. A bee does a waggle dance on the comb to show which way to fly and how far. An ant leaves a smell, called a scent trail, from food to the nest, and the others follow it. Nobody is the boss: the queen lays eggs but gives no orders.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. This supports the National Curriculum in England (Year 3 and 4 science: living things and their habitats; working scientifically through observation) and NGSS 3-LS2-1 (construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive). Facts follow the British Beekeepers' Association, the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, the Natural History Museum and Karl von Frisch's work on the dance language of bees.

The lab has six tasks. Children sort hive jobs between queen, workers and drones, drag one worker along her 5 to 6 week summer life and tap her jobs in order, read three waggle dances on a field map (angle from straight up equals angle from the sun; a longer waggle means farther food), drag a scout ant home to lay a scent trail that eight nestmates then follow, sort colony insects from loners, and judge three classmates.

Common mistakes. Children often think the queen is the boss who gives orders, that worker bees are male, that drones do the work, that all bees live in hives and make honey, or that ants find food by sight. Be careful with the word 'queen': she is the colony's egg-layer, not its ruler. Most of the world's 20,000-plus bee species, such as mason and leafcutter bees, live alone. Bumblebees live in colonies of a few hundred that last one summer.

practice.prompt: Who lays all the eggs in a honeybee hive?
practice.hint: There is only one bee in the hive with this job.
practice.explain: Only the queen lays eggs. Workers do all the other jobs, and drones are the males.

practice.prompt: In summer a queen bee lays {e} eggs a day. How many eggs does she lay in {d} days?
practice.hint: Multiply the eggs in one day by the number of days.
practice.explain: {e} × {d} = {=e*d} eggs. That is why a hive can grow to tens of thousands of bees by midsummer.

practice.prompt: A worker bee has just come out of her cell. What is her first job?
practice.hint: In the lab, where did the young worker work first: inside or outside?
practice.explain: Young workers start inside by cleaning cells. They fly out for food last, at about three weeks old.

practice.prompt: A forager bee makes {t} trips a day. On each trip she visits {f} flowers. How many flowers does she visit in a day?
practice.hint: Multiply the trips by the flowers on each trip.
practice.explain: {t} × {f} = {=t*f} flowers in one day. Thousands of foragers working together collect enough nectar to make honey.

practice.prompt: A scout ant finds a crumb. How do the other ants find it?
choices: They see it from the nest
practice.hint: What did the scout leave on the ground on her way home?
practice.explain: The scout leaves a scent trail on her way home. Other ants follow the smell to the food and add more scent.

pool.hint: Drones are different from both the queen and the workers.
pool.explain: Drones are the male bees. They have no sting and do not fetch food.

pool.prompt: Which is true about the queen bee?
choices: She lays eggs but gives no orders
She tells each worker what to do
She fetches most of the food
pool.hint: Think about her one big job.
pool.explain: The queen's job is laying eggs. Workers share out the other jobs among themselves; nobody gives orders.

pool.prompt: A waggle dance points straight up the comb. Which way should the bees fly?
pool.hint: On the comb, 'up' stands for something in the sky.
pool.explain: Straight up on the comb means 'fly towards the sun'. A dance pointing right of up means fly that much right of the sun.

pool.prompt: Two dances point the same way. One waggle is much longer. What does that tell the bees?
pool.hint: In the lab, which flower matched the long waggle?
pool.explain: A longer waggle run means the food is farther away. The angle gives the way; the length gives the distance.

pool.prompt: Which insect lives alone, not in a colony?
pool.hint: Not every kind of bee lives in a hive.
pool.explain: A mother mason bee nests alone. Most kinds of bee live alone, while every kind of ant lives in a colony.

pool.hint: Which bees in the hive are the males?
pool.explain: All worker bees are female. The males are the drones.

pool.prompt: A bumblebee nest has {w} workers. {g} of them are out fetching food. How many workers are in the nest?
pool.hint: Take the workers who are out away from all the workers.
pool.explain: {w} − {g} = {=w-g} workers in the nest, keeping the young warm, feeding them and guarding. Bumblebee colonies are much smaller than honeybee hives.

pool.prompt: A worker bee guards the door from day {a} to day {b}. How many days is that, counting both?
pool.hint: Subtract, then add 1 because both the first and last days count.
pool.explain: {b} − {a} + 1 = {=b-a+1} days. After guarding, she flies out to fetch food for the rest of her life.

pool.prompt: What happens to an ant scent trail when no ants walk on it?
pool.hint: Each ant that walks the trail adds more smell.
pool.explain: Scent fades. Ants keep a trail strong only while it leads to food, so an empty food spot is soon forgotten.
